name: Ringing tank
description: A tuned circuit, the heart of every radio: a coil (L = 7.5) and a capacitor (C = 1.5) meet at a metal strip's left end, and the strip's right end is grounded. At $t = 5$ your supply steps the coil's far end from 0 to its level. The coil's current overshoots, and the strip's end rings about the supply's level with a period of about 23 (the strip and its contact add a little to the capacitor). The strip is the circuit's resistor: its carriers' collisions turn each swing's energy into heat, and the ringing dies away. Make the ringing's amplitude between 4.5 and 9 (its oscillation at the period 23, over three periods from $t = 5$ to $74$).

reality.represents: A tuned LC circuit damped by a resistor: its Q

remarks.line: The resistor sets the ringing's decay
remarks.detail: The tank's energy swings between the coil and the capacitor and leaks into the strip as heat; across the tank, the more the strip resists, the longer it rings (Q = R√(C/L) for a parallel resistor).
The strip's resistance is no number in a formula: its carriers' collisions with the lattice take the energy, the Joule heat of every real resistor.
The strip and its contact add about 0.3 to the capacitor, so the tank rings a little slower than 1/√(LC) says, as stray capacitance detunes real circuits.
The coil and the capacitor are ideal lumped parts with no losses of their own; a real coil's wire resists and its core heats, so only the strip damps here.

remarks.line: A classical metal, a semiconductor by its ratios
remarks.detail: The carriers are classical particles at the lattice's temperature bouncing off fixed ion cores (the Drude model). A real metal's electrons are a degenerate quantum gas whose own ratios (plasma oscillations per collision, screening per free path) the model cannot afford; its carriers have a lightly doped semiconductor's ratios (the Scales section names which), which conducts by the same laws.

The strip is infinitely long along z, its carriers lines of charge moving as one: currents are per unit length, and the noise is larger than a real conductor's, whose carriers move independently along its length.

electrodes.label: strip, left end (the tank's node: the coil from your supply, the capacitor to ground)
